headline: Trump says US will stop paying Israel after end of 2026 under a deal with Netanyahu
dek: Trump said he and PM Benjamin Netanyahu 'made a deal months ago' that the US gives Israel '$4 billion a year' and 'by the end of this year we won't be paying Israel', adding 'Now we'll help Israel if they need it' and that Israel can buy its own weapons. Fox notes the current agreement provides…
sources: US President Donald Trump, on Fox News' Fox & Friends, reported by Reuters
fault_line: Is this a real break in the US-Israel funding relationship, or an Election-Day line that a 'we'll help if they need it' qualifier quietly undoes?

sections.what_happened: Trump said he and PM Benjamin Netanyahu 'made a deal months ago' that the US gives Israel '$4 billion a year' and 'by the end of this year we won't be paying Israel', adding 'Now we'll help Israel if they need it' and that Israel can buy its own weapons. Fox notes the current agreement provides about $3.8 billion annually through 2028, and that timing/terms of any change have not been detailed in the remarks provided. Trump framed the move partly as removing a talking point used by Democrats/left-wing politicians to criticise Republicans.
sections.what_verified: Reuters T1 family carries the verbatim quote; Fox News (interview origin) has NO declared tier in the registry and is NOT counted. JPost, Arab News, Straits Times, Al Arabiya and others carry the same Reuters copy = 1 family, not additional corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: Strongest counterpoint: no Israeli government confirmation and no published agreement in any report checked; Fox itself notes the current $3.8bn/yr agreement runs through 2028 and that timing/terms are undetailed; Netanyahu has previously spoken only of gradually phasing out reliance on US military aid, not of a 2026 cut-off. Trump's own qualifier ('we'll help Israel if they need it', 'if it did need the aid, he would keep it going' per Fox) leaves the cut reversible. Social reaction (Fox News IG post, 2.9K likes / 330 comments) is heavily sceptical ('I'll believe it when I see it', 'election-time Hail Mary') -- commentary, not evidence.
sections.why_matters: Trump, on Election Day morning, says the $4bn-a-year tap to Israel stops at year's end -- 'they don't need it.' The quote is real and on camera. The deal behind it is not shown: no Israeli confirmation, no document, and the current agreement runs to 2028. A break, or a line for election day?
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW (Reuters 2026-11-03; Fox News Election-Day Fox & Friends interview; AJ liveblog 13:42 GMT = 17:42 ; Gulf News liveblog 17:46 ) -- Trump says US will stop paying Israel after end of 2026 under a deal with Netanyahu

totw_analysis: Our read: Trump, on Election Day morning, says the $4bn-a-year tap to Israel stops at year's end -- 'they don't need it.' The quote is real and on camera. The deal behind it is not shown: no Israeli confirmation, no document, and the current agreement runs to 2028. A break, or a line for election day? The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is this a real break in the US-Israel funding relationship, or an Election-Day line that a 'we'll help if they need it' qualifier quietly undoes?
